headline: Tools quantify spatial and single-molecule signals while testing what dynamical models identify
label: Spatial Quantification And Identifiability
summary: Six preprints pair finer spatial and molecular quantification with explicit tests of what temporal and operator models can identify from snapshot data.
synthesis: The items share an emphasis on quantification that is explicit about its assumptions. TileScope scores gene and program spatial relationships beyond colocalization using enrichment, correlation, cross-correlation and boundary analyses. PixAQ attributes pixels to individual markers probabilistically rather than using shared masks in imaging mass cytometry. MaCADEMIA and MIST address single-molecule data, the former covering detection, counting and mobility, the latter linking trajectory dynamics, emitter properties and cellular context into a phenotype space. Two items concern identifiability: one separates temporal delay from amplitude attenuation in endometrial decidualization, and scJDO2 estimates score and flow Jacobian operators via entropic optimal transport while examining what local operators can and cannot identify. The previous deconvolution and trajectory-inference tools are not represented in these items.
